prompt: A student implements 3-SAT to IS but **forgets the triangle edges**, keeping only edges between complementary literals and a target equal to the clause count. What goes wrong?

options.text: Nothing; the consistency edges alone enforce correctness
options.explanation: Without triangles, an independent set can take several vertices from one clause and none from another, so a set as large as the number of clauses no longer means 'one per clause'.

options.text: Some unsatisfiable formulas now map to yes-instances
options.explanation: Correct. For all 8 clauses over x1, x2, x3 (unsatisfiable), the 12 positive-literal vertices have no edges among them, so an independent set of size 8 exists.

options.text: Some satisfiable formulas now map to no-instances
options.explanation: Removing edges only makes independent sets easier to find, so a yes-instance stays yes. The failure is in the other direction.
Dropping edges makes it faster, not slower. The problem is correctness, not running time.

workedExample: Removing triangle edges allows several picks from one clause while other clauses are ignored. For all eight sign patterns on three variables, the formula is unsatisfiable, yet all twelve positive occurrences are mutually nonconflicting if only consistency edges remain. The target of eight is then reachable. The reverse direction fails even though every original yes-instance remains yes.

prompt: Apply the 3-SAT to IS construction to the **unsatisfiable** formula made of all 8 clauses over x1, x2, x3 (each clause rules out one assignment). What is the size of the **maximum** independent set in the resulting 24-vertex graph?

options.explanation: Any single vertex is an independent set, so the maximum is at least 1.
Nothing limits picks to one per variable; picks are one per clause, and many clauses can share a true literal.

Correct. An independent set picks at most one true literal per clause from a consistent assignment, so its maximum size equals the most clauses one assignment can satisfy. Every assignment falsifies exactly one of the 8 clauses, so the answer is 7.
An independent set of size 8, one per clause, would mean the formula is satisfiable, but it isn't.

workedExample: Each independent set selects compatible literals from distinct clauses, so its picks extend to an assignment satisfying those clauses. Conversely, any assignment gives one pick from each clause it satisfies. Every assignment to the three variables falsifies exactly one of the eight sign-pattern clauses and satisfies the other seven. That is why the maximum independent set has seven vertices.
